source.title: Frame Representation Hypothesis: Multi-Token LLM Interpretability and Concept-Guided Text Generation
source.authors: Pedro Valois; L. S. Souza; Erica K. Shimomoto; Kazuhiro Fukui

record.tranche_reason: The study measures the ranks of multi-token word representations in LLMs, bearing conceptually on whether representations are one-dimensional or multi-dimensional. It does not reproduce Toy Models of Superposition or test feature interference.
record.gate_note: The rank analysis in Section 5.1 bears on V6. The concept-guided decoding experiments intentionally steer generation and do not test spontaneous superposition or its geometry. The paper does not test sparse-autoencoder recovery, canonicality, neuron polysemanticity, or toy-model feature competition; cited claims are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It takes the Linear Representation and Superposition Hypotheses as given. Postulate 4.1 treats tokens as linear combinations of more concepts than dimensions, and the Figure 3 overlap is explained by superposition rather than tested. On that basis it builds a word/concept 'frame' framework and a guided-decoding method. Its one empirical check is the rank of the matrix formed by the distinct token unembedding vectors of a multi-token word. That is linear independence of different tokens' output vectors in a d≥1024 space, which is expected almost trivially. It is not a measure of whether a model feature is an irreducibly multi-dimensional object, so it does not bear on V6's 1-D vs multi-D question. The remaining experiments deliberately steer generation and report the method's effect.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors propose the Frame Representation Hypothesis, which extends the Linear Representation Hypothesis by treating multi-token words as frames of token vectors and concepts as Procrustes/Fréchet means of word frames. They report that over 99% of words are full-rank, and that word frames project onto their OMW concept frames. They also show that Top-k Concept-Guided Decoding exposes gender and language biases and harmful outputs. They call the work an initial exploration.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures ranks of multi-token word representations in LLMs and uses WordNet-derived concepts; it does not use the original toy-network feature training or measure sparsity-dependent interference.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported rank behavior varies with lemma token count; Phi 3 has a rapid rank decrease beyond 5 tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: Token unembedding vectors composing OMW lemmas of up to 3-4 tokens are near-maximally linearly independent across Llama 3.1, Gemma 2 and Phi 3. Rank drops for longer lemmas, especially in Phi 3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unembedding vectors of the distinct tokens forming a word are linearly independent, so words can be modeled as frames of token vectors.

fits_no_version.finding: Word frames project positively onto their OMW synset Concept Frames, while random frames have near-zero projection (Figure 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: WordNet synset structure is linearly reflected in LLM unembedding geometry for multi-token words.

record.peer_reviewed: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The paper gives no uncertainty estimates for the rank results. Per-family rank values are presented in a figure rather than reported numerically in the text. The authors note lower ranks for longer lemmas in Phi 3.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweeps, interference or geometry.
No neuron-level analysis or capacity allocation.
No analysis of the causes of polysemantic neurons.
No measurement of feature spread across neurons and no SAE/dictionary recovery. The Figure 3 UMAP overlap is attributed to superposition without a test.
No test of whether model features are 1-D directions or irreducible multi-dimensional objects. Word frames are built by stacking token vectors by construction.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites Toy Models of Superposition only as background and assumes superposition in Postulate 4.1. Its rank result concerns stacked distinct token vectors, so it does not distinguish 1-D from multi-dimensional features in the V6 sense. The reader's V6 supports/limits_scope labels should be dropped.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse features exceeding dimensions, interference, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes neuron polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity indicates superposition.
Feature spread across neurons and recovery of sparse features with a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.

The study tests whether multi-token word representations contain multiple independent directions, but does not test whether those directions are the units superposed, or compare one-dimensional and multidimensional superposed feature models.

rows.subject: all tested model families (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured the matrix rank of token unembedding vectors for OMW lemma word frames.

conditions.value: OMW; aggregate across tested model families

rows.measure: Proportion of words with full-rank token-vector matrices
rows.value: 99.8% of words fit the frame representation; the figure caption says over 99% of words are full-rank
rows.note: The study reports this as an aggregate result, not a per-model percentage.
rows.check: Linear independence of distinct tokens' unembedding vectors is not evidence about whether superposed features are 1-D or multi-D. A word frame is the authors' construction, not a feature found in the model. Also, 99.8% is the authors' inference that the frame representation 'fits' words. It comes from near-full rank for lemmas of 1-4 tokens; it is not a directly measured full-rank proportion.

rows.value: figure only; text states a rapid rank decrease beyond token count of 5
rows.note: The text attributes the lower rank for longer lemmas partly to Phi 3 having a high proportion of lemmas with large token counts.
rows.check: The rank decrease for Phi 3 lemmas of 5+ tokens concerns long compound expressions, where repeated tokens can lower rank. It does not bear on any version.
